analysis.title: Meritage Homes Corp. (MTH) 3Q26 Recap: Operational and Capital Discipline in Focus as Visibility to Demand Further Declines
key_insights: GS keeps Buy and a $82 12-month price target on MTH (1.0x NTM tangible book value per share, unchanged) vs $64.49 price, 27.2% upside, while cutting estimates.
2026 EPS estimate cut to $4.25 from $4.75, 2027 to $4.30 from $5.20, 2028 to $5.50 from $6.85. 2026 revenue cut to $4,949.1mn from $5,270.2mn.
Demand is inelastic: 3Q sales moderated and the decline continued into October as affordability and macro uncertainty weigh on buyers. MTH is prioritizing margin over volume.
Specs per community are at about 5 months of supply, up modestly vs 2Q and at the mid-point of the 4-6 month target. About one-third of specs are completed, in line with the target.

Regional demand: strength in Dallas, Houston, South Florida and Jacksonville, weakness in San Antonio, Austin, California, Denver and Arizona. Buyer FICO scores, DTIs and LTVs are all near historical norms.

3Q gross margin was hurt by elevated incentives, more rate buydowns and loss of operating leverage. Stick-and-brick costs per sq ft were down nearly 5% YOY. Management flagged tariffs, transportation and labor as near-term headwinds, and land is expected to stay elevated through 2027 at least.

Management closed out five communities with sales to institutional build-to-rent partners, in communities where it expects no near-term improvement. Impairments were recorded in 3Q, and the remaining homes close in 4Q, 1Q and 2Q at roughly 0% margin.
GS models 4Q adjusted gross margin (incl. amortized interest) at 16.8%, down 206bps YOY, and 2027 at 17.0%, down a further 56bps. 4Q HB EBIT margin is modeled at 6.0%, down 238bps YOY.
GS models 4Q sales pace of 2.8/month, 4Q HB revenue down 13% YOY (closings down 10%, ASP down 3%), and 2027 HB revenue up 5% with a flat sales pace of 3.2/month.
Capital allocation: management prioritizes an investment grade rating, liquidity, leverage in the low-20% range and the dividend. 2026 land spend outlook cut to under $1.5bn with $1.0bn spent YTD.
GS cut its 4Q share repurchase estimate to $26mn from $54mn and projects $161mn in 2027 vs the prior $55mn per quarter. It forecasts CFO of $376mn in 2026 and $211mn in 2027.

GS sees a path to upward revisions if conditions improve ahead of the selling season, citing the passing of the mid-term elections, a possible resolution in the Middle East, lower rates and inflation, better consumer confidence and easy comps. It says its 2027 estimates could be conservative.
Scenario analysis: upside case $96 (18.8x 2027 EPS), downside case $51 (13.5x 2027 EPS). GS sees favorable risk/reward.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Buy and the $82 target (1.0x NTM tangible book value per share) despite EPS cuts, citing capital discipline and a potential recovery into the spring selling season.

sector_views.rationale: Demand is inelastic and visibility is low as affordability and macro uncertainty weigh on buyers. Underlying buyer credit quality is intact and demand could recover quickly if rates and inflation ease.

earnings_insights: MTH 3Q26 reported (30 Oct 2026 recap): gross margin hurt by elevated incentives, rate buydowns and loss of operating leverage. Impairments on the build-to-rent community close-outs were recorded in 3Q.
GS estimates: 4Q HB revenue down 13% YOY, 4Q adjusted gross margin 16.8% (down 206bps YOY), 4Q HB EBIT margin 6.0% (down 238bps YOY).
risk_factors: Incentives stay higher for longer, pressuring margins.
Greater than expected inflation in land, labor or materials.
Economic expansion comes in below GS expectations.
Delays or limits from permitting and construction restricting community growth.
Tariffs and transportation costs are near-term headwinds.
geopolitical: Report cites a potential resolution to the situation in the Middle East as a possible tailwind for rates, inflation and consumer confidence.

tension_points.bull_case: Buyer financial profiles (FICO, DTIs, LTVs) are near historical norms, so demand could recover quickly if rates and inflation ease. GS sees easy comps and a better spring set-up than investors expect after the mid-term elections and a possible Middle East resolution.
tension_points.bear_case: Demand is inelastic, sales moderated in 3Q and continued to decline into October. Incentives, rate buydowns and lost operating leverage pressure margins, with land, tariff, transportation and labor costs elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Incentives staying higher for longer, or inflation in land, labor or materials above expectations, would pressure margins and undercut the Buy case.

theme_stances.key_argument: A decline in rates, inflation and better consumer confidence after the mid-terms could make for a better spring selling season than investors expect.
theme_stances.evidence: could make for a better set-up into the spring vs investors' expectations

theme_stances.key_argument: Management is balancing profitability and capital structure through lower land spend, build-to-rent close-outs and an investment grade priority.
theme_stances.evidence: Disciplined Capital Allocation Leaves MTH Well Positioned for an Eventual Recovery
